newsitem.title: USA: Judge overturns Mass. congressional primary.
newsitem.headline: Judge overturns Mass. congressional primary.

text.p: In a stunning reversal, a Massachusetts judge declared William Delahunt the winner of the Democratic primary in a bitterly fought battle to fill the seat being vacated by retiring congressman Gerry Studds, newspapers reported on Saturday.
Only hours before the judge's ruling late on Friday, Philip Johnston, the original winner in the Sept. 17 ballot, was campaigning with first lady Hillary Clinton.
Johnston, a liberal who lacked funds for a television campaign in the primary, initially won by a 206 vote margin. After a recount in selected districts, his lead shrunk to 175.

But Norfolk Superior Court Judge Elizabeth Donovan ruled, after a review of some 900 challenged ballots, that Delahunt, the Norfolk district attorney, actually won the race by 108 votes. She ordered Secretary of State William Galvin to print new ballots with Delahunt's name.
But the battle to be on the Nov. 5 ballot may not be over. Johnston told reporters he would appeal to the state's highest court on Monday.
